# GitHub Actions

| Workflow | Runs on | Does | Phase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ci.yml` | Pull requests | One job per component, each running only when its folder changes: `jtf` (ruff, unit tests, `dagster definitions validate`; also when `notebooks/` or `warehouse/dbt/` changes, since ruff lints the notebooks and the tests load the dbt project into Dagster; its pytest also runs the warehouse rules that need only dbt's manifest, such as the layers' reads), `warehouse` (unit tests, an empty `dbt build` and the SQL rules over compiled SQL, in a PR dataset that reads no real data; data tests run on real data in the pipeline), `dashboard` (Vitest), `deploy` (`terraform validate` and `plan`); `e2e_tests` when `jtf/` or `warehouse/` changes | 1 |
| `release.yml` | Merge to `main` | Build the image once, deploy to dev, then prod after approval, then post-deploy steps. Phase 1: build, then point the capture job and the Dagster code location at the digest | 1 |
| `model-release.yml` | Change to `deploy/models.yaml` | Move the `production` alias and rewrite the pointer file | 3 |

GitHub reaches GCP only through Workload Identity Federation; no service account keys exist. The `warehouse` job reads four repository variables: `GCP_DEV_PROJECT` and `GCP_REGION` (as in `.env`), and `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` and `GCP_CI_DEV_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (`deploy/bootstrap`'s outputs of those names). It runs as `ci-dev`: it makes its own datasets, `ci_<run id>_<attempt>_<layer>`, an empty ODS among them (`jtf ci create`), builds every model on them with `dbt build --empty` and the unit tests under the `ci` target, which fails any query reading over 100 MB, compiles every model again without `--empty` (which hides each table behind a subquery of its own) and runs the SQL rules over that, and drops them even when a step fails; their tables expire after a day in case a run dies first. Pull requests from forks get no identity token, so the job skips them. Only `ci.yml` may act as `ci-dev`: bootstrap maps GitHub's `job_workflow_ref` claim to a `workflow` attribute and binds the account to that file alone, not to any workflow in the repository (on a pull request GitHub runs the PR's own copy of it, so this pins the file, not its contents). The dev project also caps what queries scan per day, 200 GiB in all and 100 GiB per account, people included (`envs/dev`), so a runaway loop can't burn the free tier. Backfills are not a GitHub Action: they are launched from the prod Dagster UI.
